headline: High: shared filesystem and permissive tool use make Windsurf vulnerable to Authelia-mediated prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading misexecution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can expose auth-gated content through OIDC/ForwardAuth, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, and shares state via local filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge where content from Authelia-fed pages or files can be treated as instructions by Windsurf. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected content is copied into Windsurf workspace files or MCP inputs, then injected instructions can reach Windsurf's tool loop.
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled, then malicious instructions in shared files can trigger actions without extra approval.
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Keep Authelia outputs out of shared workspace files.
Use a separate non-shared directory for any copied content.
Require manual review of any file or MCP payload before tool use.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for content flowing from Authelia to Windsurf.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles authentication flows and broad network egress, while Windsurf reads and writes workspace files, uses clipboard, and handles model-provider keys. Because Windsurf shares state via local filesystem, sensitive auth artifacts or open files can leak from the shared workspace into Windsurf outputs or upstream APIs. The profiles support a default-path leakage risk, but not enough for high.
conditions: IF Authelia-related secrets or tokens are stored in files that Windsurf can read, then those values may be sent to the model proxy or MCP servers.
IF clipboard sync is used between the agents, then copied auth material can be exposed to Windsurf.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Clear clipboard after copying auth material.
Restrict Windsurf access to a non-sensitive directory.
Rotate any token that was present in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce file-level secret redaction before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing behavior, while Windsurf can execute shell commands, modify git state, write files, and spawn subprocesses. Windsurf also shares state via local filesystem, so both agents can mutate the same project artifacts without a locking primitive being documented. That makes conflicting writes and git corruption plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, then concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Windsurf modifies git state while Authelia-driven automation also updates files, then repository history can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Use separate worktrees per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Add a manual checkpoint before commits.
requires-engineering: introduce file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit auth-related decisions or content that Windsurf may ingest through files, MCP, or copied text. Windsurf then has authority to edit files, run shell commands, and modify git state, so an incorrect upstream output can cascade into real actions. Because Windsurf's tool loop is agentic and auto-execute is opt-in, the pathway is dangerous by default but not fully automatic enough for critical.
conditions: IF Windsurf treats Authelia-derived text as authoritative, then mistaken instructions can be executed as shell or git actions.
IF auto-execute is enabled, then a bad upstream decision can propagate without a human review step.
mitigations: Require human review before any shell or git action.
Disable auto-execute.
Separate factual outputs from executable commands.
Add verification checks for Authelia-derived content.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and Windsurf handles open files and source code with broad egress. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a limited compliance concern is supportable. I cite both profiles because the risk arises from their combined handling of auth and code data, but the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf workspace files, then retention and logging policies must be checked before use.
IF Authelia is configured for a regulated identity domain, then downstream handling in Windsurf must match that domain's policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces.
Review retention settings for any copied auth artifacts.
Document the data class allowed in the shared workflow.
Use a separate environment for regulated identities.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data flows.
